feedback: The questionnaire focusses mainly on the issue of representation or diversity and inclusion. While this has sparked debate regarding certain movie remakes I feel that the question of originality is ignored. Race seems to be put at the forefront of the little mermaid controversy, and this is seen as the main motivation to watch or not watch the movie. The issue however is that Disney has been making remakes for a while as opposed to new or original content. The little tweaks or changes they make in live-action movies such as race-switching seems to be used as a replacement for new and original stories. Fairy tales and their remakes, especially Hans' Christian Andersen's have always been retouched to convey certain morals based on societal changes (for example compare the original moral of the Red Shoes fairy tale to its later movie adaptation). Even the original religious moral conveyed in the somewhat tragic end of the original little mermaid story is not conveyed in Disney's first movie adaptation. However Disney's more recent movie adaptations don't seem to follow such a tradition. Instead they seem to profit from politicised social issues to create social buzz. The casting of diverse characters by Disney in itself then seems like an insincere cash-grab rather than a new or profound message that reflects the changing nature of our society.  I think that this is what will ultimately affect further Disney sales.
